clue.text: Copper on trial agitated in dock

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: agitated letters are stirred up and thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A policeman, upset by his trial, is standing in the dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' is the element CU, not the policeman; 'agitated' scrambles TRIAL into RTAIL. 'Dock' is the verb, to cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock a tail or wages is to cut it short, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Sadly, quiet pair gone to seed

indicators.note: sadly here means in a sorry state, so the letters are messed about

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A quiet couple has sadly gone to seed, past their best.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gone to seed' reads as decline, but 'seed' alone is the definition, with 'to' as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pip is a small fruit seed, and the kind found in a citrus fruit is a specific example.

clue.text: A vice in business here?

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the abbreviation for business

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
a vice is a sin

explanation.surface: A question about where you might find vice going on as a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' does double duty in the surface reading, but read as wordplay the whole clue also describes a gambling house, where vice is the business.
explanation.definitionFit: A gambling house is a place where the vice of betting is a business, hence the whole clue describes it.

clue.text: Can reckon, with reorganisation, to run team and gain a point

indicators.note: reorganisation means the letters of run team are reordered

parts.note: E (east) is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A manager reorganises the running of a team and gains a point, showing financial savvy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with reorganisation' rearranges RUN TEAM into NUMERAT; 'gain' adds E, a compass point.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone numerate is competent with figures, able to reckon and calculate.

clue.text: Bourse in English is good for exchanges with fellow countrymen

definitions.text: Bourse in English is good for exchanges with fellow countrymen

indicators.note: exchanges means the letters of the phrase swap places among themselves

explanation.surface: A stock market in English is good for trading with compatriots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bourse' is a continental stock exchange; 'exchanges' tells you to swap around all fifteen letters of BOURSE IN ENGLISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendliness towards those living nearby, the spirit that makes dealings with one's fellows go well.

clue.text: Increase put Milly in a tizzy

indicators.note: a tizzy is a state of agitation, so the letters are flustered into a new order

explanation.surface: Something increased and left a woman called Milly in a flap.
explanation.definitionFit: To multiply is to grow in number or amount, a direct synonym for increase.

clue.text: He gets up and is found on the staircase

definitions.meaning: a person who rises from bed, as in an early bird
the vertical board between two treads of a stair

explanation.surface: Someone who gets up is spotted on the stairs.
explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is a person who rises from bed; the other is the upright part of a step.

clue.text: The acrobatic ones posture intricately?

indicators.note: intricately suggests the letters are twisted into an elaborate new pattern

explanation.surface: A question whether acrobats hold their poses in an intricate way.
explanation.definitionFit: Companies of performers, such as circus acrobats, travel as touring groups.

clue.text: Large rodent shuffling in a rut

indicators.note: shuffling mixes the letters of the following words into a new order

explanation.surface: A big rodent stuck shuffling along in a groove.
explanation.definitionFit: The coypu, a big South American water rodent, is also known by this name.

clue.text: Fancy I'll get tiny part, touring America

indicators.note: touring means going round, so the outer pieces enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe
an ion is a tiny charged particle

explanation.surface: A fancy that an actor gets a bit part while on a tour of America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Touring America' suggests travel, but 'touring' is the container signal; 'get' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy is a figment of imagination, a false perception or delusion.

clue.text: Reject eggs — family start to gag! They're rotten!

indicators.note: to reject is to turn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: nits are the eggs of lice
kin means family

indicators.note: start to means just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Someone refuses rotten eggs, and the family starts to gag at the smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reject' turns the lice eggs round, giving STIN; 'They're' only links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stinking, in its informal sense, means very bad or rotten.

clue.text: I get put out about two robbers starting to break in

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go around the pair of initials
put out means the letters of put are disturbed
two means the initial is taken twice
starting gives the first letter of the word robbers

explanation.surface: Someone is put out by two robbers starting to break into the house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' scrambles the letters of put to UPT; 'two' doubles the initial taken from 'robbers starting', and 'about' sets that pair inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to burst in forcibly, the same idea as breaking in.

clue.text: Should it go off, I'm to be turning in my grave?

definitions.text: Should it go off, I'm to be turning in my grave?

parts.words: Should it go off, I'm to be turning in my grave?
parts.note: a device that detonates would leave one dead and buried, hence the grim joke about turning in one's grave

explanation.surface: A rhetorical question about being so outraged one would spin in the grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A delayed explosive device whose going off would kill, sending the victim to the grave.

clue.text: Retreat of flier in slowest fashion, circling the north

indicators.note: circling means the rearranged letters wrap around the letter for north
to fashion is to shape, so the letters are remodelled

parts.note: N is the abbreviation for north

explanation.surface: A bird flies back to its retreat in the slowest manner, circling north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashion' turns SLOWEST into OWLSEST, and 'circling' wraps that round N.
explanation.definitionFit: The hollow home of a nocturnal bird is its retreat, a flier's hideaway.

clue.text: Having money, reserves pads

parts.note: a note is paper money
to book is to reserve

explanation.surface: Someone with cash reserves a flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pads of paper for jotting are bound writing books, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Giving Arab sack upset sector in the factory

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the whole run upside down, reading it backwards

parts.note: a Moor was a North African of Arab descent
loot is plunder, what is taken in a sack of a city

explanation.surface: An upset part of the factory where an Arab was given the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns MOOR + LOOT end to end; 'sack' is plunder, not dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: A room in a factory where implements are made or stored is one section of the works.

clue.text: Its movement can cause sudden drop in this species of spider

definitions.text: Its movement can cause sudden drop
definitions.meaning: a hinged hatch in a floor that drops someone when opened
a spider that hides in a burrow sealed by a hinged lid

explanation.surface: A spider whose movement causes a sudden fall.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a hinged floor hatch through which one drops and the name of a burrowing spider.

clue.text: Fluster, in confusion? Soothing is required

indicators.note: confusion means the letters are jumbled into a different order

explanation.surface: When flustered and confused, calm is called for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calming and peaceful is soothing, a close synonym.

clue.text: It's sheer malice, positioning base in arid surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the word for arid wraps around the other piece

parts.note: arid means dry
base means morally low, evil

explanation.surface: A tale of wickedness, setting up a base camp in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'base' looks like a camp or foundation but means low and wicked; 'positioning' and 'in' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Devilry is wicked mischief or cruelty, the behaviour of a devil.

clue.text: Kicked heels — left one toe bruised and inflamed

indicators.note: bruised means battered, so the letters are knocked about

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
inflamed skin looks red

explanation.surface: Someone kicked their heels with a bruised and swollen toe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bruised' rearranges I and TOE into OITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Kicking one's heels is an idiom for hanging about idly, which is to dawdle or linger.

clue.text: Encroachment on fashionable thoroughfare

parts.note: in means fashionable
a road is a thoroughfare

explanation.surface: Building encroaches on a trendy street.
explanation.definitionFit: Making an advance into someone else's territory is an encroachment.

clue.text: Animal a well-drilled, smooth runner, once set free

parts.note: an ass is a donkey, an animal
oil comes from drilled wells and is a lubricant that makes things run smoothly

explanation.surface: A well-trained, fast animal is released.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Well-drilled' suggests training but means pumped from an oil well. 'Once' marks the definition as an archaic word.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic verb meaning to absolve or release from sin or guilt.

clue.text: Attack in connection with some games of tennis

parts.note: on means about or concerning
a set is a group of games in tennis

explanation.surface: An attack linked with a few tennis matches.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of an assault, an attack.

clue.text: On Arctic manoeuvres, drug supplied

indicators.note: on manoeuvres means the letters move about into a new position

explanation.surface: Drugs were supplied to troops on Arctic manoeuvres.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic is a drug that dulls the senses, an example of the class.

clue.text: In the main, endless fresh food is cooked

indicators.note: cooked means prepared, so the letters are altered into a new order
endless means the last letter of food is cut off

explanation.surface: Fresh food is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' trims FOOD to FOO; 'is cooked' rearranges that with FRESH. 'The main' is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic word for the open sea, so being in it means out at sea.

clue.text: African soldier with monarch dressed in oriental robe

parts.note: A is an abbreviation for African

indicators.note: dressed in means the monarch's letter is wrapped inside the robe

parts.note: a sari is a robe worn in South Asia
K is the abbreviation for king, a monarch

explanation.surface: An African soldier accompanies a king dressed in an eastern robe.
explanation.walkthrough: SARI is the Indian draped garment; K for king goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An askari is a local soldier or police officer in East Africa.

clue.text: Told off half-back, in the past

indicators.note: off means set wrong, so the letters are rearranged
back means the word for half is read backwards

parts.note: semi means half

explanation.surface: Someone was told off by a half-back, back in the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-back' looks like the football position, but SEMI (half) is turned back to IMES; 'off' rearranges TOLD to OLDT.
explanation.definitionFit: Days gone by, the bygone era, are referred to as the past.
